CITf OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 17, 2025-5:00 P.M.
1  City Halt Council Chamber

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmembers Hampton and Madison)

  CLOSED SESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:03 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session items:

  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (one potential case)

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Councilmember Hampton  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  arrived at 6:07 p.m.  Name of Case: Harrell, C. v. City of Pasadena
  Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No. 20STCV06887

  The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

  Vice Mayor Rivas reported that she is participating remotely under
  the "just cause" provisions of the Brown Act on the basis ofchildcare
  needs and stated that no one over 18 years of age is in the room
  with her.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:35
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Jones.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas (via teleconference)
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison (arrived at 7:04 p.m.)
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting to be adjourned in memory
  of Don Nollar, longtime Pasadena resident and former City
  employee, and spoke on Mr. Nollar's work revamping the City's
  General Plan and his volunteer work with the Civitan Club.

  Council Minutes  1  03/17/2025
 SPECIAL ITEM  PRESENTATION BY JEFFREY PRANG, LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY ASSESSOR, ON PROPERTY IMPACTS RELATED TO
  THE EATON FIRE AND RELATED ASSESSOR SERVICES FOR
  AFFECTED RESIDENTS

  Jeffrey Prang, LA County Assessor, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the County Assessor Office programs available to
  residents impacted by the recent wildfires, and provided clarification
  on tax assessments for properties with fire related damage, and
  responded to questions.

  Following brief discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the presentation was received and filed.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City Council
MATTERS NOT ON THE  to agendize AB392 for discussion and continued to express
AGENDA  concerns related to the Anthony McClain shooting.
Councilmember Madison  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, inquired about the status of the
arrived at 7:04 p.m.  City's underground wiring project, oversight of the City's police
  department, and establishing a fair process pertaining to sale of the
  710 stub properties.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, requested for the City Council to agendize
  discussion of the City's response to the Eaton Fire and aftermath,
  and she urged the City Council to retain the remote public comment
  option for public meetings.

  Kristina Nichols, Pasadena resident, shared details of her recent
  encounter with a coyote and expressed concerns regarding an
  increased presence of coyotes in her neighborhood.

  The following individuals provided comments on divestment and
  apartheid:

  Dylan Bannon, Pasadena resident
  Michael Flynn, Pasadena resident

  In response to public comment, Mayor Gordo stated that the AB392
  will be discussed at the Public Safety Committee meeting in April,
  and that an update from the Police Department has not yet been
  scheduled but will occur at the Public Safety Committee at a future
  meeting.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Lyon reported that
  the Pasadena Public Health Department, in conjunction with wildlife
  officers at Pasadena Humane, are conducting a study of coyote
  behavior around the City.

the meeting at 7:26 p.m.  HOLLY STREET BRIDGE SEISMIC RETROFIT PROJECT AND
  APPROVE PROJECT DESIGN PLANS (Public Works Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find on the basis of the whole record before it (including the
  initial study and any comments received), that there is no substantial
  evidence that the project will have a significant effect on the
  environment and that the Mitigated Negative Declaration reflects the
  lead agency's independent judgement and analysis; and, therefore
  adopt a Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Holly Street Bridge
  Seismic Retrofit project pursuant to the California Environmental
  Quality Act, and adopt a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
  Program; and
  (2) Approve the Holly Street Bridge Seismic Retrofit project
  reflected in the Design Plan.

  Nina Chomsky, Pasadena resident, expressed support for the
  item, and raised questions regarding federal funding for the
  project, potential impacts the closure of the bridge would have
  during Rose Bowl displacement events, and advocated for
  additional public meetings to ensure that neighboring residents
  are informed.

  In response to public comment, Greg de Vinck, Public Works
  Director, reported that the proposed project will not change the
  bridge aesthetically. He reported that the main purpose is to wrap
  and strengthen the columns for seismic loading. Brent Maue, Acting
  City Engineer, reported that the City anticipates full funding to be
  secured from Caltrans.

  MOTION:  It was moved by Councilmember Hampton, seconded by
  Councilmember Masuda, to approve the staff recommendation.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Hampton, Lyon, Madison,

RECOMMENDATIONS  REQUEST FROM THE PASADENA RENTAL HOUSING BOARD
FROM OFFICERS AND  FOR THE CITY COUNCIL TO DIRECT THE CITY ATTORNEY TO
DEPARTMENTS  PREPARE AN ORDINANCE WITHIN 60 DAYS ADOPTING ALL
  AVAILABLE TENANT PROTECTIONS PROVIDED IN THE ELLIS
City Manager  ACT (GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 7060 ET SEQ.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is not subject to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to section 21065 of
  CEQA Guidelines Sections 15060(c)(2), 15060(c)(3), and 15378,
  and as such, no environmental document pursuant to CEQA is
  required; and
  (2) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an ordinance within 60 days
  adopting all available tenant protections provided in the Ellis Act
  (Government Code Section 7060 Et Seq.).

  Helen Morales, Rent Stabilization Director, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the Ellis Act provisions, and responded to questions.

  In response to Councilmember Madison's inquiry regarding rental
  properties in the City that would be subject to Ellis Act protections,
  Deputy City Attorney Martinez clarified that the protections would
  apply to rental units citywide, including rent regulated units.

  Discussion ensued regarding the 10-year period for the first right of
  refusal for evicted tenants if a property returns to the rental market,
  the City Charter provisions and the Pasadena Rental Housing Board
  ("PRHB") not being authorized under the law to adopt Ellis Act
  protections (only elected legislative bodies able to act and adopt by
  ordinance), and how the punitive damage provision could potentially
  result in inequity if a property has a short tenancy.

  In response to Councilmember Madison's inquiry regarding why the
  PRHB opted for the 10-year period, Rent Stabilization Director
  Morales reported that City Charter Article XVIII requires that such
  protections be adopted to the maximum extent permitted by law.
  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns about defaulting the
  matter to the City Council under Charter Article XVIII provisions,
  which pertain to the PRHB.

Council Minutes  13  03/17/2025
   Councilmember Lyon advocated for further legal analysis of City
  Charter Article XVIII, the Ellis Act, and the discretions available to
  the City Council and the PRHB, as well as issues related to the 180-
  day limitation to implement Article XVIII, and the the effect of Section
  1806(c) (Right of Return and First Right of Refusal). He also
  emphasized the need for additional legal analysis from City
  Attorney's Office that provides the City Council with sufficient
  information regarding staff's positions and recommendations to
  make decisions.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding parameters
  to prevent the original tenants from taking advantage or somehow
  transferring the Right of Return and First Right of Refusal provision
  to others, Rent Stabilization Director Morales reported that the Ellis
  Act requires the original tenant to live in the unit if the tenant were to
  exercise their rights under the Act. She added that the City can
  implement a regulation allowing landlords to evict the tenant if the
  person found occupying the unit is not listed on the lease.

  Councilmember Madison made a motion to shorten the first right of
  refusal after returning to the rental market period from 10 years to 5
  years. Motion failed due to lack of second.

  Councilmember Lyon reiterated the need for a thorough legal
  analysis of the interplay between City Charter Article XVIII Section
  1806(c) and Section 1806(d).

  Joseph Bautista, Pasadena resident, expressed support for City
  staff to further analyze City Charter Article XVIII and the potential
  leeway municipalities may have when implementing the Ellis
  Act.

   In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry, Rent Stabilization
  Director Morales reported that the Ellis Act requires the elected
  governing body for the jurisdiction where rental restrictions exist to
  adopt a resolution or ordinance to establish and adopt the Ellis Act
  provisions in order for these protections to become effective and
  available to tenants in the City.
